<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Further Discussion of Related Work</h3>

<div id="A1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Reward Machines (RMs)</span>
Reward Machines (RMs) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib55" title="" class="ltx_ref">Icarte et al., 2022</a>)</cite> provide a structured representation of reward functions.
However, their primary objective differs fundamentally from that of Reward Design and, consequently, HRD.
RMs aim to help RL agents exploit its reward structure to improve sample efficiency during learning.
In contrast, HRD focuses on producing hierarchical reward structures that maximize policy fitness, which in our case is measured by the policy’s alignment with behavioral specifications.
In addition to the different goals, the underlying representations are also distinct.
RMs rely on temporal logic formulas to define structured rewards, while HRD extends the original Reward Design Problem <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Singh et al., 2009</a>)</cite> and defines hierarchical reward functions inspired by established HRL frameworks (e.g., options and feudal hierarchies).
Building on RMs, <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib56" title="" class="ltx_ref">Furelos-Blanco et al., 2023</a>)</cite> introduced Hierarchies of Reward Machines (HRMs) to increase the expressivity of RMs and further accelerate policy convergence in some cases.
Again, while HRMs aim to improve learning efficiency, HRD focuses on enabling the capture of complex behavioral specifications through a hierarchical reward structure, particularly for long-horizon tasks.
Because RMs or HRMs do not focus specifically on reward design from human input, the ease of specifying RMs or HRMs from human input remains to be investigated.
In contrast, for the HRD problem using the L2HR algorithm and human evaluations, we have empirically shown that language models can leverage the structure of HRD to generate hierarchical rewards that induce policies well-aligned with complex behavioral specifications.
An interesting future direction is to explore novel approaches that leverage complementary strengths of RMs and HRD to facilitate both sample-efficient and human-aligned AI.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">LLM-RL Hybrid Agents</span>
Although our work focuses on hierarchical RL paradigms, there is a growing body of research on hybrid agents that combine large language models (LLMs) for subtask selection with reinforcement learning for subtask execution <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ahn et al., 2022</a>; <a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al., 2023</a>)</cite>.
HRD can help contribute to this line of work in two key ways.
First, it can provide a formalism for analyzing reward design in hybrid LLM-RL systems.
Second, it can inform the development of advanced methods that leverage LLMs with hierarchical reward structures, combining the <span id="A1.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">expressivity</span> of hierarchical rewards with a <span id="A1.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">user-friendly</span> reward design process.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
<section id="A2" class="ltx_appendix">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix B </span>Theoretical Analysis</h3>

<section id="A2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.1. </span>Low- and High-Level Decision Models</h4>

<section id="A2.SS1.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">B.1.1. </span>Low-Level MDP Models</h5>

<div id="A2.Thmtheorem1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proposition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_smallcaps ltx_title_theorem">Proposition 0 (Low-level MDP Models).</h6>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{p}=(\mathcal{S},\mathcal{A},T,\gamma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>T</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>γ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{p}=(\mathcal{S},\mathcal{A},T,\gamma)</annotation></semantics></math> be a world model, <math id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}</annotation></semantics></math> a set of options, and <math id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{L}:\mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{O}\times\mathcal{A}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>ℝ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{L}:\mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{O}\times\mathcal{A}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}</annotation></semantics></math> a low<span id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text">-</span>level reward.
For a fixed option <math id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o\in\mathcal{O}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o\in\mathcal{O}</annotation></semantics></math>, the tuple <math id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{L,o}=(\mathcal{S},\mathcal{A},T,r_{L}(\cdot,o,\cdot),\gamma,h_{o})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>o</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>T</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>o</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>γ</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>o</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{L,o}=(\mathcal{S},\mathcal{A},T,r_{L}(\cdot,o,\cdot),\gamma,h_{o})</annotation></semantics></math> defines an MDP, where <math id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{o}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>o</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{o}</annotation></semantics></math> is the horizon determined by the option’s termination condition <math id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta(\cdot,o)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>o</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta(\cdot,o)</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.SSS1.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A2.SS1.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.SSS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text">The state space is <math id="A2.SS1.SSS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}</annotation></semantics></math> and the action space is <math id="A2.SS1.SSS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{A}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The transition function <math id="A2.SS1.SSS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> is the transition function of the world model and is Markovian.
Defining <math id="A2.SS1.SSS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{L,o}(s,a)=r_{L}(s,o,a)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>o</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>o</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{L,o}(s,a)=r_{L}(s,o,a)</annotation></semantics></math> produces a Markov reward function that depends only on the state-action pair.
Thus, the tuple satisfies the four standard components of an MDP.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS1.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">B.1.2. </span>High-Level SMDP Model</h5>

<div id="A2.Thmtheorem2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proposition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_smallcaps ltx_title_theorem">Proposition 0 (High-level SMDP Model).</h6>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.Thmtheorem2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="A2.Thmtheorem2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{p}=(\mathcal{S},\mathcal{A},T,\gamma,h)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>T</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{p}=(\mathcal{S},\mathcal{A},T,\gamma,h)</annotation></semantics></math> be a world model, <math id="A2.Thmtheorem2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}</annotation></semantics></math> a set of options, and <math id="A2.Thmtheorem2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{H}:\mathcal{O}\times\mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{O}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>ℝ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{H}:\mathcal{O}\times\mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{O}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}</annotation></semantics></math> the high<span id="A2.Thmtheorem2.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text">-</span>level reward. Then, <math id="A2.Thmtheorem2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{H}=(\mathcal{O}\times\mathcal{S},\mathcal{O},T_{H},r_{H},\gamma,h)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{H}=(\mathcal{O}\times\mathcal{S},\mathcal{O},T_{H},r_{H},\gamma,h)</annotation></semantics></math> forms a semi-MDP, where <math id="A2.Thmtheorem2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{H}:\mathcal{O}\times\mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{O}\rightarrow\Delta(\mathcal{O}\times\mathcal{S}\times\mathbb{N})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>ℕ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{H}:\mathcal{O}\times\mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{O}\rightarrow\Delta(\mathcal{O}\times\mathcal{S}\times\mathbb{N})</annotation></semantics></math> defines the joint distribution over the next augmented state and transit time, where <math id="A2.Thmtheorem2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ℕ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{N}</annotation></semantics></math> is the set of natural numbers.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.SSS2.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A2.SS1.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.SSS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text">A semi-MDP (SMDP) requires (1) a set of states, (2) a set of actions, (3) for each state-action pair, an expected discounted reward, and (4) a well-defined joint distribution over the next state and transit time <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sutton et al., 1999</a>)</cite>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.SSS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.SSS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">We define the state space as the Cartesian product <math id="A2.SS1.SSS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}\times\mathcal{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}\times\mathcal{S}</annotation></semantics></math>, combining the previous option <math id="A2.SS1.SSS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o^{-}\in\mathcal{O}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>o</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o^{-}\in\mathcal{O}</annotation></semantics></math> and the current environment state <math id="A2.SS1.SSS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s\in S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s\in S</annotation></semantics></math>.
The action space is the set of options <math id="A2.SS1.SSS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The reward function for each state-action pair <math id="A2.SS1.SSS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\big((o^{-},s),o\big)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>o</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>o</mi><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\big((o^{-},s),o\big)</annotation></semantics></math> is given by the provided high-level reward <math id="A2.SS1.SSS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{H}(o^{-},s,o)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>o</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>o</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{H}(o^{-},s,o)</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.SSS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.SSS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">To define the transition dynamics, consider the transition probability from a given augmented state <math id="A2.SS1.SSS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(o^{-},s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>o</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(o^{-},s)</annotation></semantics></math> upon selecting an option <math id="A2.SS1.SSS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>o</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o</annotation></semantics></math>.
Let <math id="A2.SS1.SSS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the state upon option termination and <math id="A2.SS1.SSS2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> the number of timesteps to reach <math id="A2.SS1.SSS2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The transition function <math id="A2.SS1.SSS2.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{H}</annotation></semantics></math> is defined as:</span></p>
<table id="A2.EGx4" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A2.E6"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.E6.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle T_{H}(o,s^{\prime},k|o^{-},s,o)=\sum_{\tau:\ (o^{-},s)\rightarrow(o,s^{\prime})}\text{Pr}(\tau;\pi_{L,o})\cdot\mathbb{I}_{\{k=|\tau|\}}\cdot\beta(s^{\prime},o)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>o</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msup><mi>o</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>o</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.688em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>o</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>o</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></munder></mstyle><mtext>Pr</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo>;</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>o</mi></mrow></msub><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>𝕀</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>k</mi><mo rspace="0em">=</mo><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>β</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>o</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle T_{H}(o,s^{\prime},k|o^{-},s,o)=\sum_{\tau:\ (o^{-},s)\rightarrow(o,s^{\prime})}\text{Pr}(\tau;\pi_{L,o})\cdot\mathbb{I}_{\{k=|\tau|\}}\cdot\beta(s^{\prime},o)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS2.p3.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.SSS2.p3.2.1" class="ltx_text">where <math id="A2.SS1.SSS2.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> is any trajectory that starts in state <math id="A2.SS1.SSS2.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> after option <math id="A2.SS1.SSS2.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o^{-}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>o</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o^{-}</annotation></semantics></math> and reaches state <math id="A2.SS1.SSS2.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> via option <math id="A2.SS1.SSS2.p3.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>o</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A2.SS1.SSS2.p3.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{Pr}(\tau;\pi_{L,o})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>Pr</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>o</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{Pr}(\tau;\pi_{L,o})</annotation></semantics></math> is the probability of trajectory <math id="A2.SS1.SSS2.p3.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> under policy <math id="A2.SS1.SSS2.p3.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{L,o}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>o</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{L,o}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A2.SS1.SSS2.p3.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\tau|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\tau|</annotation></semantics></math> is the number of timesteps taken by the trajectory.
Given a specific <math id="A2.SS1.SSS2.p3.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau=(o_{t-1},s_{t},o_{t},s_{t+1},\ ...\ ,o_{t+\eta-1},s_{t+\eta})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>o</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo lspace="0.500em">,</mo><msub><mi>o</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>η</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>η</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau=(o_{t-1},s_{t},o_{t},s_{t+1},\ ...\ ,o_{t+\eta-1},s_{t+\eta})</annotation></semantics></math> and knowing that <math id="A2.SS1.SSS2.p3.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o_{t-1}=o^{-}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>o</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>o</mi><mo>−</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o_{t-1}=o^{-}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS1.SSS2.p3.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o_{t},\ ...\ ,o_{t+\eta-1}=o" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.667em">,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo lspace="0.500em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>o</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>η</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>o</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o_{t},\ ...\ ,o_{t+\eta-1}=o</annotation></semantics></math>, the probability of the trajectory is given by:</span></p>
<table id="A2.EGx5" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A2.E7"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(7)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.E7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\text{Pr}(\tau;\pi_{L,o})=\prod_{i=0}^{\eta-1}\Big(\sum_{a}\pi_{L,o}(a|s_{t+i})T(s_{t+i+1}|s_{t+i},a)\Big)\cdot\prod_{i=0}^{\eta-2}\Big(1-\beta(s_{t+i+1},o)\Big)" displaystyle="true"><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∏</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></munderover></mstyle><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">(</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mi>a</mi></munder></mstyle><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>o</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" movablelimits="false">∏</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></munderover></mstyle><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>o</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\text{Pr}(\tau;\pi_{L,o})=\prod_{i=0}^{\eta-1}\Big(\sum_{a}\pi_{L,o}(a|s_{t+i})T(s_{t+i+1}|s_{t+i},a)\Big)\cdot\prod_{i=0}^{\eta-2}\Big(1-\beta(s_{t+i+1},o)\Big)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS2.p3.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.SSS2.p3.3.1" class="ltx_text">The first product accounts for the probabilities of transitioning through the intermediate states under <math id="A2.SS1.SSS2.p3.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{L,o}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>o</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{L,o}</annotation></semantics></math> and the environment’s underlying dynamics <math id="A2.SS1.SSS2.p3.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math>.
The second product ensures that the option does not terminate at intermediate states prior to reaching <math id="A2.SS1.SSS2.p3.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math>.
As all four conditions are satisfied, the tuple <math id="A2.SS1.SSS2.p3.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{H}</annotation></semantics></math> forms a valid SMDP.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS1.SSS3" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">B.1.3. </span>High-Level MDP Model</h5>

<div id="A2.SS1.SSS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Alternatively, the high-level process can be modeled as an MDP if <span id="A2.SS1.SSS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">single-step</span> high-level rewards <math id="A2.SS1.SSS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{H}^{step}(o_{t-1},s_{t},o_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>o</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{H}^{step}(o_{t-1},s_{t},o_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> are defined.
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang and Whiteson, 2019</a>)</cite> was the first to model high-level decision-making as an MDP within the options framework.
While our formulation differs from theirs, we draw inspiration from their use of <span id="A2.SS1.SSS3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">single-step</span> high-level rewards and demonstrate that the high-level process in our setting can also be modeled as an MDP.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proposition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_smallcaps ltx_title_theorem">Proposition 0 (High-level MDP Model).</h6>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.Thmtheorem3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="A2.Thmtheorem3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{p}=(\mathcal{S},\mathcal{A},T,\gamma,h)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>T</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{p}=(\mathcal{S},\mathcal{A},T,\gamma,h)</annotation></semantics></math> be a world model, <math id="A2.Thmtheorem3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}</annotation></semantics></math> a set of options, and <math id="A2.Thmtheorem3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{H}^{step}:\mathcal{O}\times\mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{O}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>ℝ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{H}^{step}:\mathcal{O}\times\mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{O}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}</annotation></semantics></math> a “single-step” high<span id="A2.Thmtheorem3.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text">-</span>level reward.
Then, <math id="A2.Thmtheorem3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{H}^{step}=(\mathcal{O}\times\mathcal{S},\mathcal{O},T_{H}^{step},r_{H}^{step},\gamma,h)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mi>γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{H}^{step}=(\mathcal{O}\times\mathcal{S},\mathcal{O},T_{H}^{step},r_{H}^{step},\gamma,h)</annotation></semantics></math> forms an MDP, where <math id="A2.Thmtheorem3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{H}^{step}:\mathcal{O}\times\mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{O}\rightarrow\Delta(\mathcal{O}\times\mathcal{S})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{H}^{step}:\mathcal{O}\times\mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{O}\rightarrow\Delta(\mathcal{O}\times\mathcal{S})</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.SSS3.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A2.SS1.SSS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.SSS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">We again define the state space as <math id="A2.SS1.SSS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}\times\mathcal{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}\times\mathcal{S}</annotation></semantics></math> and the action space as <math id="A2.SS1.SSS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The transition function is defined as:
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="T_{H}^{step}(o,s^{\prime}|o^{-},s,o)=\sum_{a}\pi_{L}(a|s,o)\cdot T(s^{\prime}|s,a)\cdot\mathbb{I}_{\{o^{\prime}=o\}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>o</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msup><mi>o</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>o</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>a</mi></msub><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>o</mi><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>T</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>𝕀</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>o</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>o</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{H}^{step}(o,s^{\prime}|o^{-},s,o)=\sum_{a}\pi_{L}(a|s,o)\cdot T(s^{\prime}|s,a)\cdot\mathbb{I}_{\{o^{\prime}=o\}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Termination condition is not modeled in the transition function, since option selection occurs at every step.
The reward function is <math id="A2.SS1.SSS3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{H}^{step}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{H}^{step}</annotation></semantics></math>, which satisfies the MDP requirements.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.SSS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">As a side note, we can derive the expected SMDP high-level reward from the single-step rewards as follows:</p>
<table id="A2.EGx6" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A2.E8"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(8)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.E8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle r_{H}(o^{-},s,o)\doteq\mathbb{E}[\sum_{i=1}^{k}\gamma^{i-1}{r_{H}^{step}}_{t+i}|\mathcal{E}(o^{-},o,s,t)]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>o</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>o</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≐</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>k</mi></munderover></mstyle><mrow><msup><mi>γ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>r</mi><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow><mrow></mrow></mmultiscripts></mrow></mrow><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>o</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>o</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle r_{H}(o^{-},s,o)\doteq\mathbb{E}[\sum_{i=1}^{k}\gamma^{i-1}{r_{H}^{step}}_{t+i}|\mathcal{E}(o^{-},o,s,t)]</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS3.p3.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A2.SS1.SSS3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{E}(o^{-},o,s,t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>o</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>o</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{E}(o^{-},o,s,t)</annotation></semantics></math> is the event of initiating option <math id="A2.SS1.SSS3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>o</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o</annotation></semantics></math> in state <math id="A2.SS1.SSS3.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> at timestep <math id="A2.SS1.SSS3.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> following option <math id="A2.SS1.SSS3.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o^{-}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>o</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o^{-}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A2.SS1.SSS3.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> is the random variable denoting the number of steps after which the initiated option <math id="A2.SS1.SSS3.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>o</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o</annotation></semantics></math> terminates, as determined by its termination condition <math id="A2.SS1.SSS3.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.2. </span>Policy Learning with Hierarchical Rewards</h4>

<div id="A2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Given hierarchical reward functions in <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem1" title="Definition 0 (Low-level Reward). ‣ 3.1. Low-level and High-level Reward Models ‣ 3. Hierarchical Reward Design ‣ Hierarchical Reward Design from Language: Enhancing Alignment of Agent Behavior with Human Specifications" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Definition</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a> and <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem3" title="Definition 0 (High-level Reward). ‣ 3.1. Low-level and High-level Reward Models ‣ 3. Hierarchical Reward Design ‣ Hierarchical Reward Design from Language: Enhancing Alignment of Agent Behavior with Human Specifications" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Definition</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a>, agents can learn low- and high-level policies through interactions with the environment under their respective decision-making models.</p>
</div>
<section id="A2.SS2.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">B.2.1. </span>Low-Level Policy Learning</h5>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each option <math id="A2.SS2.SSS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o_{i}\in\mathcal{O}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o_{i}\in\mathcal{O}</annotation></semantics></math>, the low-level decision-making process can be formulated as an MDP <math id="A2.SS2.SSS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{L,o_{i}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{L,o_{i}}</annotation></semantics></math> (see <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem2" title="Proposition 0 (Low-level MDP Models). ‣ 3.1. Low-level and High-level Reward Models ‣ 3. Hierarchical Reward Design ‣ Hierarchical Reward Design from Language: Enhancing Alignment of Agent Behavior with Human Specifications" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Proposition</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a>).
Let <math id="A2.SS2.SSS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{L,o_{i}}(s,a)=r_{L}(s,o_{i},a)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{L,o_{i}}(s,a)=r_{L}(s,o_{i},a)</annotation></semantics></math> represent the reward function for option <math id="A2.SS2.SSS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS2.SSS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{o_{i}}(a|s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{o_{i}}(a|s)</annotation></semantics></math> a policy in the MDP.
The objective for low-level policy learning is to maximize the cumulative discounted rewards until the termination of option <math id="A2.SS2.SSS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>

<p id="A2.SS2.SSS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A2.SS2.SSS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{o}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>o</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{o}</annotation></semantics></math> is the horizon determinied by the option’s termination condition <math id="A2.SS2.SSS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta(\cdot,o_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta(\cdot,o_{i})</annotation></semantics></math>.
Standard RL algorithms for MDPs can be directly used to obtain low-level policies.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">B.2.2. </span>High-Level Policy Learning (SMDP)</h5>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">When the high-level decision-making is modeled by an SMDP, the high-level policy <math id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{H}(o|o^{-},s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mrow><msup><mi>o</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{H}(o|o^{-},s)</annotation></semantics></math> selects options only at the termination of the previous option, operating on a coarser temporal scale compared to the low-level policy <math id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{L}(a|s,o)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>o</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{L}(a|s,o)</annotation></semantics></math>.
Let <math id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u=0,\dots,h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u=0,\dots,h</annotation></semantics></math> index the <span id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">high-level</span> decision points, and define <math id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta_{o_{u}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>η</mi><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>u</mi></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta_{o_{u}}</annotation></semantics></math> as the number of primitive timesteps taken to execute option <math id="A2.SS2.SSS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o_{u}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o_{u}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Then, the high-level policy learning objective is:</p>

<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">B.2.3. </span>High-Level Policy Learning (MDP)</h5>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p1" class="ltx_para">

movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mi>h</mi></munderover></mstyle><msup><mi>γ</mi><mi>t</mi></msup><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>o</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\pi_{H}^{step}(o|o^{-},s)=\arg\max_{\pi}\mathbb{E}_{(o_{t-1},s_{t})\sim T_{H}^{step},\,o_{t}\sim\pi}[\sum_{t=0}^{h}\gamma^{t}r_{H}^{step}(o_{t-1},s_{t},o_{t}))|\mathcal{M}_{H}^{step}]</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Similarly, we let <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o_{-1}=o_{\#}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>o</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>#</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o_{-1}=o_{\#}</annotation></semantics></math>.
When the termination condition is known, as in our setting, the high-level policy can be expressed as: <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{H}^{step}(o|o^{-},s)\doteq\beta(s,o^{-})\pi_{H}(o|o^{-},s)+(1-\beta(s,o^{-}))\mathbb{I}_{(o=o^{-})}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>π</mi><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mrow><msup><mi>o</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≐</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>o</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mrow><msup><mi>o</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>o</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝕀</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>o</mi><mo>−</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{H}^{step}(o|o^{-},s)\doteq\beta(s,o^{-})\pi_{H}(o|o^{-},s)+(1-\beta(s,o^{-}))\mathbb{I}_{(o=o^{-})}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A2.SS2.SSS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{H}(o|o^{-},s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mrow><msup><mi>o</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{H}(o|o^{-},s)</annotation></semantics></math> specifies the policy at decision points.
This allows leveraging known termination conditions to constrain policy rollouts.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.3. </span>Expressivity of HRD</h4>

<div id="Thmproperty1a" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_property">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_smallcaps ltx_title_theorem">Property 1.</h6>
<div id="Thmproperty1a.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmproperty1a.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmproperty1a.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Certain specifications on sub-task selection can be expressed through <math id="Thmproperty1a.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{r}_{H}(o^{-},s,o)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>H</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>o</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>o</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{r}_{H}(o^{-},s,o)</annotation></semantics></math>, but they cannot be expressed by a flat reward function: <math id="Thmproperty1a.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{r}_{flat}(s,a)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>l</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{r}_{flat}(s,a)</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A2.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text">Consider two distinct subtask sequences, {<math id="A2.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o_{1}\rightarrow o_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>o</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msub><mi>o</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o_{1}\rightarrow o_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>} and {<math id="A2.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o_{1}^{\prime}\rightarrow o_{2}^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>o</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msubsup><mi>o</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o_{1}^{\prime}\rightarrow o_{2}^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math>} such that after executing either <math id="A2.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>o</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="A2.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o_{1}^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>o</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o_{1}^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math>, the agent arrives at the same state <math id="A2.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s^{*}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The designer’s specification is for the agent to follow the corresponding subtask sequences: execute <math id="A2.SS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>o</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> after <math id="A2.SS3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>o</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o_{2}^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>o</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o_{2}^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> after <math id="A2.SS3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o_{1}^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>o</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o_{1}^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math>.
A flat reward function <math id="A2.SS3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{r}_{flat}(s,a)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>l</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{r}_{flat}(s,a)</annotation></semantics></math> cannot represent this specification, as the reward signal depends only on the current state and action, and cannot distinguish whether the agent reached <math id="A2.SS3.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> via <math id="A2.SS3.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>o</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="A2.SS3.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o_{1}^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>o</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o_{1}^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math>.
In contrast, with HRD’s high-level reward function, we can specify the ordering even in <math id="A2.SS3.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> by defining <math id="A2.SS3.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{r}_{H}(o^{-}\mkern 1.5mu{=}\mkern 1.5muo_{1},s\mkern 1.5mu{=}\mkern 1.5mus^{*},o\mkern 1.5mu{=}\mkern 1.5muo_{2})&gt;\tilde{r}_{H}(o^{-}\mkern 1.5mu{=}\mkern 1.5muo_{1},s\mkern 1.5mu{=}\mkern 1.5mus^{*},o\neq o_{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>H</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>o</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo rspace="0.358em">=</mo><msub><mi>o</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0.358em" rspace="0.358em">=</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0.358em" rspace="0.358em">=</mo><msub><mi>o</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>H</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>o</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo rspace="0.358em">=</mo><msub><mi>o</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0.358em" rspace="0.358em">=</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo>≠</mo><msub><mi>o</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{r}_{H}(o^{-}\mkern 1.5mu{=}\mkern 1.5muo_{1},s\mkern 1.5mu{=}\mkern 1.5mus^{*},o\mkern 1.5mu{=}\mkern 1.5muo_{2})&gt;\tilde{r}_{H}(o^{-}\mkern 1.5mu{=}\mkern 1.5muo_{1},s\mkern 1.5mu{=}\mkern 1.5mus^{*},o\neq o_{2})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS3.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{r}_{H}(o^{-}\mkern 1.5mu{=}\mkern 1.5muo_{1}^{\prime},s\mkern 1.5mu{=}\mkern 1.5mus^{*},o\mkern 1.5mu{=}\mkern 1.5muo_{2}^{\prime})&gt;\tilde{r}_{H}(o^{-}\mkern 1.5mu{=}\mkern 1.5muo_{1}^{\prime},s\mkern 1.5mu{=}\mkern 1.5mus^{*},o\neq o_{2}^{\prime})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>H</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" ∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="Thmproperty2a" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_property">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_smallcaps ltx_title_theorem">Property 2.</h6>
<div id="Thmproperty2a.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmproperty2a.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmproperty2a.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Certain specifications on sub-task execution can be expressed through <math id="Thmproperty2a.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{r}_{L}(s,o,a)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>L</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>o</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{r}_{L}(s,o,a)</annotation></semantics></math>, but they cannot be expressed by a flat reward function: <math id="Thmproperty2a.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{r}_{flat}(s,a)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>l</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{r}_{flat}(s,a)</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.3" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A2.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">Consider a setting where the behavioral specification explicitly depends on the current option <math id="A2.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>o</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o</annotation></semantics></math>.
Such specifications cannot be represented using a flat reward function, as the reward signal <math id="A2.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{r}_{flat}(s,a)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>l</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{r}_{flat}(s,a)</annotation></semantics></math> is identical for all option values.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>

<section id="A3" class="ltx_appendix">

            <span id="alg1.l1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Input:</span> World model <math id="alg1.l1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{p}" display="inline" <math id="alg1.l1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><annotation <section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Experimental Details</h3>

<section id="A4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.1. </span>Further Domain Details</h4>

<div id="A4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Rescue World</span> is a variant of the RW4T domain <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Orlov Savko et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, a configurable testbed for simulating disaster response scenarios in which a first responder deploys robots to collect scattered supplies and deliver them to designated areas.
For our experiments, we configure the environment with a single robot and represent the world using a discrete grid-based layout (<a href="#A4.F8.sf1" title="In Figure 8 ‣ D.1. Further Domain Details ‣ Appendix D Experimental Details ‣ Hierarchical Reward Design from Language: Enhancing Alignment of Agent Behavior with Human Specifications" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Fig.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8(a)</span></a>).
The robot must determine both <span id="A4.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">the delivery order</span> of supplies and <span id="A4.SS1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">the optimal path</span> for completing deliveries.
This setting naturally motivates a hierarchical action representation due to the need for subtask sequencing and execution.
The primitive action space <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{A}</annotation></semantics></math> includes six actions: pick, drop, and four directional movements (up, down, left, right).
The option space <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}</annotation></semantics></math> consists of multi-step pick-up and delivery macro-actions for two supply types: <span id="A4.SS1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">food</span> and <span id="A4.SS1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">medical supplies</span>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">iTHOR</span> is a simulator built within the AI2-THOR framework <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib72" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kolve et al., 2017</a>)</cite>, featuring realistic household environments where an agent can navigate and interact with everyday objects.
We use <span id="A4.SS1.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">FloorPlan 20</span> as the environment for our experiments.
In our setup, apples and eggs are spawned on one side of a long kitchen table, the sink is located on the opposite side, and a stool is positioned to the right of the table, as shown in  <a href="#S5.F4.sf1" title="In Figure 4 ‣ 5.2. Domains ‣ 5. Experiments ‣ Hierarchical Reward Design from Language: Enhancing Alignment of Agent Behavior with Human Specifications" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Fig.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4(a)</span></a>.
The option space <math id="A4.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}</annotation></semantics></math> consists of pick-up and place operations for each object type, while the action space <math id="A4.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{A}</annotation></semantics></math> includes navigation actions (move forward, turn left, turn right) and pick/place primitives.
While conducting experiments with expert-provided rewards (Sec. <a href="#A4.SS2" title="D.2. Results with Expert-Provided Rewards ‣ Appendix D Experimental Details ‣ Hierarchical Reward Design from Language: Enhancing Alignment of Agent Behavior with Human Specifications" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D.2</span></a>), we observe that inducing the agent to follow the <span id="A4.SS1.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">diversity</span> preference is highly sensitive to the reward scale.
To address this, we include additional contextual information in the LLM prompt specifically about the typical length of the options to guide more consistent reward generation.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Kitchen</span> is a single-agent variant of Overcooked, a benchmark environment originally designed for studying human-AI collaboration in kitchen tasks <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2025</a>)</cite>.
In our setting, the agent must prepare a salad using lettuce, tomatoes, and onions.
We adopt the structured option space from <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, which includes high-level options such as <span id="A4.SS1.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">chop onion</span> and <span id="A4.SS1.p3.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">combine chopped onion and chopped tomatoes</span>.
The environment also provides hard-coded low-level controllers for executing these options.
The primitive action space <math id="A4.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{A}</annotation></semantics></math> includes directional movement actions that enable interactions with countertops and other kitchen objects.</p>
</div>

<section id="A4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.2. </span>Results with Expert-Provided Rewards</h4>

<figure id="A4.T3" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="A4.T3.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 3</span>. </span><span id="A4.T3.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">
Table showing the performance of policies trained with the task reward alone and with task reward combined with expert-provided flat or hierarchical rewards.
For each metric (“High-Level,” “Low-Level,” and “Total”), we report both the cumulative returns and the percentage of policies achieving expert-level alignment.
A policy is considered expert-aligned at the high or low level if it attains the maximum possible cumulative return for that metric.
“Total” represents the sum of the task reward, high-level alignment reward, and low-level alignment reward, and a policy is deemed expert-level overall if it aligns at both levels.
</span></figcaption>
